name: v31-card-visit
description: THE CONTROL. This is the v31 game as it stood from 02/09/2026 to 04/09/2026, and it is the arm every future comparison is read against, because on 04/09/2026 Dean ruled the meeple loop in and the shipped default became rules.turn.visitCurrency 'meeple'. The knob did not go away when it stopped being an experiment; it turned around. WHAT THIS OVERLAY PUTS BACK, all of it at once, which is why it is a control and not a proposal. A visit is bought with ONE CARD FROM YOUR HAND, and the card is placed on a Notice Board, so the visitor pays in the same currency they build and grow with. The Notice Board is a BUILDING again: it has a threshold of 2 (rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold), it clogs, it is cleared by its owner spending a Harvest, and a clogged board shuts that suit's door to the whole table. SELF-VISITING IS LEGAL again (rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed, true in the shipped data and simply ignored under the meeple currency), so a seat may place its bonus card on its own board and take its own suit's action - the solitaire door that risk 2 of the v31 pass armed on purpose. The bonus slot's other half is the STANDALONE FREE DRAW 1 (rules.turn.bonusDraw) rather than Collect, so there is no way for a host to be paid for being visited and no meeple ever moves between players. The turn-start meeple spend comes back with it: meeples are spent one at a time at the START of the turn, each performing its colour's plain action and then LEAVING THE GAME, which is the drain that made two of the five colours dead. The Orchard door is DRAW 3, not Draw 2, because under a card fee a Draw 2 door hands back exactly what the free option gives for nothing - the self-cancellation law, which has no subject once a visit costs no card. The island seeds a meeple on BOTH delivery spaces of every tile (island.meeples.perDeliverySpace) rather than one on the 3 VP space, so the bag is drawn 12 / 18 / 24 deep instead of 6 / 9 / 12. WHAT IT IS FOR. Three things, in the order they will actually be wanted. (1) IT IS THE BASELINE FOR EVERY DELTA. The meeple loop was measured once, on reference-v11 seeds, and that measurement is now history rather than an instrument: the reference has been re-cut as reference-v12 and no reference-v11 number survives the boundary. Anything that wants to say 'the meeple loop bought us X' has to run this arm on reference-v12 seeds beside the default and read the pair. (2) IT IS THE REGRESSION TEST ON A LIVE CODE PATH. The 'card' branch is not dead code - the engine still carries doVisit's card half, the Notice Board's building rules, bonusDraw, the turn-start meeple spend and the threshold clog - and the only thing exercising them at scale is this overlay. A branch nothing runs is a branch that rots. (3) IT IS THE HONEST ANSWER TO 'WERE WE RIGHT?'. The meeple loop was ruled in on a measurement that was not flattering: the hook FELL, 0.41 to 0.37 per player per turn, and the game got 35-43% longer. It was ruled in on the two things that did move - the two dead meeple colours came back to life (Apiary and Dairy take 46% of door uses against 32%) and self-visiting became impossible by construction - and on the judgement that interaction per GAME rose 21% even as interaction per turn fell. That is a defensible call and it is not a settled one, so the game it replaced has to stay one flag away. READ IN THIS ORDER, and read the noise floor line before any of them. (1) THE HOOK, rival visits per player per turn, and the SELF-VISIT LINE beside it - under this overlay self-visits are legal again and took 22.2% of turns the last time anybody measured them, and an assertion that pools them with rival visits will report a healthy hook while the table plays solitaire. (2) THE BONUS MIX, where the solitaire line is the free Draw 1 rather than the empty-board Collect; it took 67.6% of turns under this arm against the default's 54.2%. (3) GAME LENGTH, which is the regression the meeple loop bought its wins with and the one number this arm is expected to win on. (4) THE DOOR MIX, where orange and cream should collapse back to the bottom, because Sow and Build spend cards and a card-fee visit charges the visitor for spending them. (5) The meeple economy, which under this arm is a faucet and a drain rather than a loop and where 'spent versus gained' is a meaningful question again. TWO WARNINGS. This overlay restores the RULES and not the CARD TEXT: W17 The Pie Shop is now keyed on the visited event as the v33 sheet retexts it ('Whenever a neighbour visits you, Draw 1'), so under this arm it pays its owner for a visit landing on their board but no longer for a cross-table sow onto one of their fields. That divergence is deliberate and is the one place where the control is not bit-identical to the game of 03/09/2026. And the bots are the reference-v12 bots throughout: they price a meeple, a Collect and a wild spend, and nothing re-tunes them when this flag flips, so a per-seat number here is the current evaluator's opinion of the old rules rather than the old evaluator's.
